attributes.action: Make Dover the designated port for all Channel small-boat disembarkations
attributes.additional_details: We believe the UK should have a clear and consistent national policy for Channel small-boat disembarkations. Dover has established infrastructure for receiving Channel arrivals and onward transfer to Home Office facilities. Concentrating routine disembarkations at a designated location would provide consistency and accountability, while avoiding disruption and additional pressure on smaller coastal towns, cities, ports and local communities.
attributes.background: We want the Government to designate Dover as the UK disembarkation point for people brought to the UK following small-boat crossings of the English Channel, rather than routinely using other UK ports or harbours, with onward transfer to designated Home Office processing facilities.

rejection.details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action that relates to a particular local area, including petitions that call for action relating to a specific port or town.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise this issue with the Home Office. You can find contact details for the Home Office here: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/contact-the-home-office
